'''''Helianthus hirsutus''''' is a North American species of [[Helianthus|sunflower]] known by the common name '''hairy sunflower'''. It is widespread across south-central Canada, the eastern and central United States, and northeastern [[Mexico]]. It ranges from [[Ontario]] south to [[Florida]], [[Coahuila]], and [[Nuevo León]], and west as far as [[Minnesota]], [[Nebraska]], and [[Texas]].<ref>{{BONAP|ref |genus=Helianthus |species=hirsutus}}</ref>

''Helianthus hirsutus'' is a perennial sometimes as much as 200 cm (almost 7 feet) tall, spreading by means of underground rhizomes. Leaves and stems are covered with stiff hairs. One plant can produce 1–7 [[flower heads]], each with 10–15 yellow [[ray florets]] surrounding 40 or more yellow [[disc floret]]s. The species grows in sunny locations in open forests or along the edges of forests.<ref>{{eFloras|1|242416632|Helianthus hirsutus |tribe=Heliantheae |first=Edward E. |last=Schilling}}</ref>

==Ecology==

''Helianthus hirsutus'' is insect pollinated and is recorded to have been visited in northern Florida by ''[[Augochlorella aurata]]'', ''[[Megachile parallela]]'', and ''[[Svastra aegis]]''. <ref>Ulyshen, M. D., K. Robertson, S. Horn, and C. Dixon. 2024. Characterization of the bee community and pollination network in a southeastern U.S. pine savanna. Frontiers in Ecology and Evolution 12:1403602.</ref>
